test: Illinois Secretary of State Written Driver's License Exam (Class D)
edition: Based on the Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 edition (Illinois Secretary of State, DSD A 112.47, printed July 2026).

exam.rules: New Illinois drivers take the written exam at a Secretary of State Driver Services (DMV) facility, together with a vision screening, when applying for an instruction permit (teens 15–17 enrolled in driver education, or anyone 17 years 3 months or older) or a first Class D license; written-test results stay valid until the permit expires. The Class D exam has at least 35 questions and you need 80% (28 of 35) to pass. It is commonly given as 15 road-sign questions (identify signs by shape, color and symbol) plus 20 multiple-choice and true/false questions on traffic laws, safe driving, crash prevention and vehicle equipment. One application fee covers three attempts at each exam within one year, and a second attempt may be allowed the same day. Anyone caught cheating fails and must wait 30 days. Oral exams can be requested in person Monday through Thursday.

questions.q: At what age can an Illinois teen enrolled in an approved driver education course first get an instruction permit?
questions.explain: Teens aged 15–17 can get an instruction permit with proof that they are enrolled (or will start within 30 days) in approved driver education.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Obtaining an Instruction Permit' (p. 16)

questions.q: A driver under 18 must hold an instruction permit for at least how long before getting a driver's license?
questions.explain: Applicants aged 15–17 must hold the permit for at least nine consecutive months with no violations.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Graduated Driver Licensing Program' (p. 18)

questions.q: How many hours of supervised practice driving must a driver under 18 log before getting a license?
questions.explain: Illinois requires at least 50 hours of supervised behind-the-wheel practice, 10 of them at night, in addition to driver education.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Obtaining an Instruction Permit' (p. 16)

questions.q: Who may supervise an Illinois instruction permit holder outside of driver education class?
options: A licensed adult aged 21 or older with at least one year of driving experience, seated in the front passenger seat
A licensed adult aged 19 or older seated in the back seat
Any licensed driver aged 18 or older seated anywhere in the vehicle
questions.explain: The supervising parent, guardian or responsible adult must be 21+, hold a valid license, have at least one year of experience and sit next to the driver.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Obtaining an Instruction Permit' (p. 16)

questions.q: During the permit phase, what are the nighttime driving restrictions on Friday and Saturday nights?
options: No driving from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m.
No driving from midnight to 5 a.m.
No driving from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
No driving from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
questions.explain: Under GDL the night restriction is 10 p.m.–6 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11 p.m.–6 a.m. Friday–Saturday (local curfews may differ).
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Graduated Driver Licensing Program' (p. 18)

questions.q: For drivers under 18, what are the nighttime driving restrictions Sunday through Thursday?
options: No driving from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
No driving from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
No driving from midnight to 6 a.m.
No driving from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
questions.explain: The GDL night restriction is 10 p.m.–6 a.m. on Sunday–Thursday nights for permit holders and initial-phase licensees.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Graduated Driver Licensing Program' (p. 18)

questions.q: During the first 12 months of the Initial Licensing Phase (or until age 18), how many passengers under age 20 may a teen driver carry, not counting siblings or the driver's children?
questions.explain: For the first 12 months or until 18, passengers under 20 are limited to one, unless they are siblings, step-siblings, children or step-children.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Graduated Driver Licensing Program' (p. 18)

questions.q: During the permit phase, what passenger limit applies?
options: Up to three passengers in total, regardless of belts
One passenger in the front seat, and no more back-seat passengers than there are safety belts
No passengers other than the supervising adult
Two passengers in the front seat and any number in the back
questions.explain: Permit holders are limited to one front-seat passenger and to the number of safety belts in the back seat.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Graduated Driver Licensing Program' (p. 18)

questions.q: A 17-year-old with a graduated license wants to use a hands-free phone to call a friend while driving. Is this legal in Illinois?
options: Yes, if the call lasts under two minutes
Yes, but only on roads posted 45 mph or less
Yes, hands-free calls are legal for all licensed drivers
No, drivers under 19 may not use any phone, even hands-free, except to report an emergency
questions.explain: Any wireless phone use, including hands-free, is banned for drivers under 19 except emergency calls to police, health care or emergency services.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Graduated Driver Licensing Program' (p. 18)

questions.q: To move out of the Initial Licensing Phase on time, a teen driver must keep a conviction-free record for how long before turning 18?
questions.explain: A conviction-free record for the six months before turning 18 is required; a conviction can extend the restrictions past 18.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Graduated Driver Licensing Program' (p. 18)

questions.q: A 19-year-old who has never been licensed and never took driver education wants a first Illinois license. What must they complete first?
options: Nothing extra; only the exams are required
A six-hour Adult Driver Education Course from a Secretary of State certified provider
A 30-hour high school driver education course
questions.explain: First-time applicants aged 18–20 without prior driver education must finish a six-hour certified Adult Driver Education Course.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'First-Time Drivers — Age 18-20' (p. 18)

questions.q: At what age can an Illinois teen apply for an instruction permit without taking a driver education course?
questions.explain: Applicants who are 17 years and 3 months or older may get a permit without enrolling in driver education.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Obtaining an Instruction Permit' (p. 16)

questions.q: Someone who moves to Illinois with a valid out-of-state license must get an Illinois license within how many days (or before the old license expires, if sooner)?
questions.explain: A new Illinois resident has 90 days to switch to an Illinois license, or less if the old license runs out sooner.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 1 Illinois Driver's License, 'Exemptions' (p. 5)

questions.q: How soon must you notify the Secretary of State after moving to a new address?
options: Only when your license is renewed
questions.explain: Address changes must be reported within 10 days of the move, in person, online or by mail.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 1 Illinois Driver's License, 'Changing the Name/Address on an Illinois Driver's License/ID Card' (p. 6)

questions.q: What minimum visual acuity is needed for an Illinois driver's license without restrictions on daylight driving?
questions.explain: The minimum is 20/40; acuity between 20/41 and 20/70 limits the driver to daylight driving only.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 2 Driver's License Exams, 'Vision Screening' (p. 13)

questions.q: A driver whose best visual acuity is 20/60 may be licensed with what restriction?
options: Driving only with another licensed adult
questions.explain: Acuity between 20/41 and 20/70 restricts the driver to daylight driving.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 2 Driver's License Exams, 'Vision Screening' (p. 13)

questions.q: How many attempts does one Illinois driver's license application fee give you to pass each exam?
questions.explain: Applicants get three attempts to pass each exam within one year of paying the application fee.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 2 Driver's License Exams, 'Driver's License Exams' (p. 13)

questions.q: What happens to an applicant caught cheating on the written exam?
options: They lose their permit for six months but may retest the same day
They get one warning and may continue
They must wait one year to retest
They fail and cannot retake the exam for 30 days
questions.explain: A cheater fails the exam and is barred from retaking it for 30 days.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 2 Driver's License Exams, 'Cheating and Bribery' (p. 13)

questions.q: A license issued to a driver under 21 expires when?
options: Three months after the driver's 21st birthday
Four years after issue, regardless of age
questions.explain: Licenses for drivers under 21 expire three months after the 21st birthday.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 1 Illinois Driver's License, 'Driver's License/ID Card Renewal' (p. 8)

questions.q: Until what age can the parent or guardian who signed consent cancel a minor's driver's license?
options: Only during the first six months of licensing
Until the driver turns 16 and a half
questions.explain: Until the teen turns 18, the parent or guardian who gave consent can ask the Secretary of State to cancel the license for any reason.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Parental Responsibility' (p. 19)

questions.q: A driver under 21 is convicted of two moving violations within 24 months. What is the result?
options: A $50 fine with no effect on the license
License suspension for at least 30 days
questions.explain: Two or more moving violations within 24 months for a driver under 21 brings a suspension of at least 30 days.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Related Laws' (p. 20)

questions.q: To receive court supervision for a traffic violation, a driver under 21 must do what?
options: Complete 50 more hours of supervised driving
Attend traffic safety school (and appear with a parent or guardian if under 18)
questions.explain: Drivers under 21 are limited to one court supervision and must attend traffic safety school; those under 18 must appear with a parent or guardian.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Related Laws' (p. 19)

questions.q: If you develop a medical condition likely to cause a loss of consciousness, how soon must you notify the Secretary of State?
options: Only if you are involved in a crash
Within 10 days of becoming aware of it
questions.explain: Drivers must report such a condition within 10 days; failing to do so can lead to cancellation of the license.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 1 Illinois Driver's License, 'Medical Report' (p. 10)

questions.q: Under Illinois law, an adult driver's license may be suspended after how many traffic violation convictions within 12 months?
questions.explain: Three traffic violation convictions in a 12-month period can result in suspension (two in 24 months for drivers under 21).
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 8 Revocation, Suspension, Denial and Cancellation, 'Suspension' (p. 60)

questions.q: What are the minimum liability insurance limits required for vehicles in Illinois?
options: $25,000 per person injured, $50,000 per crash for injuries, $20,000 property damage
questions.explain: Illinois minimums are $25,000 for one person's injury/death, $50,000 for more than one person, and $20,000 for property damage.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 13 Owning a Vehicle, 'Mandatory Insurance' (p. 98)

questions.q: What is the penalty for a conviction of driving without the required insurance?
options: Loss of driving privileges for one month
Loss of driving privileges for at least three months and a $100 reinstatement fee
questions.explain: A mandatory insurance conviction brings at least a three-month suspension and a $100 reinstatement fee, with no driving permit available.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Safety Responsibility Law' (p. 55)

questions.q: What must you do at this sign?
options: Slow down and proceed without stopping if no one is coming
Stop only if another vehicle is approaching
Come to a complete stop, then yield to pedestrians and traffic before going
questions.explain: This octagon requires a full stop at the stop line, or before the crosswalk or intersection if there is no line.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 65)

questions.q: What does this sign require?
options: Speed up to enter traffic ahead of others
Merge without changing speed because others must yield to you
Slow down and give the right of way to vehicles and pedestrians, stopping if necessary
Always come to a full stop
questions.explain: This triangle means you must let all traffic and pedestrians go first, stopping if needed.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 65)

questions.q: Where would you typically see this sign and what does it mean?
options: At a school; children may be crossing
At a closed parking lot; slow down
Before a toll plaza; prepare to stop
At a one-way street or wrong-direction ramp entrance; you may not enter
questions.explain: This sign marks one-way roadways and ramps you are not allowed to enter.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 65)

questions.q: If you see this sign while driving, what has happened?
options: You are entering a one-lane bridge
The road ahead is closed for construction
You are traveling the wrong direction and must turn back safely
questions.explain: This sign tells you your vehicle is going the wrong way, often on an expressway ramp or one-way street.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 66)

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: The maximum legal speed under good conditions is 55 mph
The suggested speed for trucks only
The minimum speed is 55 mph at all times
questions.explain: Speed limit signs show the maximum speed; you must go slower when conditions require.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 66)

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Left turns are allowed only on red
Left turns are not allowed here
Keep left of the island ahead
questions.explain: A red circle with a slash means the action shown is not allowed; here, a left turn.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 66)

questions.q: At an intersection with this sign, what is prohibited?
options: Turning when the signal is green
Turning while the signal shows red
Driving straight through on red after a stop
questions.explain: This sign forbids a right turn on red (and a left on red from one one-way street to another).
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 67)

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Detour in the direction of the arrow
Passing is allowed in the direction of the arrow
The road ahead turns in the direction of the arrow
Traffic on this street may travel only in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: A one-way sign means traffic may move only the way the arrow points.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 67)

questions.q: What does this sign require when you approach a traffic island or median?
options: Drive to the left of the obstruction
Drive to the right of the obstruction
Make a U-turn around the island
questions.explain: This sign tells you to keep to the side shown by the arrow, the right, around islands, medians or obstructions.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 67)

questions.q: What does this sign mean on a two-lane road?
options: Do not stop on the shoulder
You may not pass other vehicles here
Trucks may not use this lane
questions.explain: This sign marks a section where passing is prohibited; yellow no-passing lines are also used.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 68)

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: You must pass slower vehicles now
Use extra care because the lane narrows
The no-passing zone has ended; you may pass when it is safe
questions.explain: This sign marks the end of a no-passing zone; pass only when safe.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 68)

questions.q: Who may park in a space marked with this sign?
options: Vehicles displaying disability license plates or parking placards
Only electric vehicles that are charging
Any vehicle for up to 15 minutes
Any vehicle with its hazard lights on
questions.explain: These spaces are reserved for vehicles showing Persons with Disabilities plates or parking placards (qualifying veteran plates are also allowed).
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Other Special Signs' (p. 74)

questions.q: How should you treat this sign at a railroad crossing?
options: Like a yield sign: give the right of way to any approaching train
Like a stop sign that requires stopping every time
questions.explain: A crossbuck is considered a yield sign; you must yield to oncoming trains and railroad equipment.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Railroad Crossings' (p. 81)

questions.q: This plaque appears below a stop sign. What does it tell you?
options: Traffic from every direction must stop; the first to stop goes first
You may turn right without stopping
Only cross traffic has to stop
questions.explain: It means every approach has a stop sign; drivers proceed in the order they stopped.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 65)

questions.q: On a multilane highway, what does this sign mean?
options: All traffic must stay right except trucks
Right turns only from the right lane
Drivers going slower than the normal flow should use the right lane
questions.explain: Slower drivers on multilane highways must use the right lane.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 67)

questions.q: What does this warning sign mean?
options: Turn right at the next intersection
The road curves to the right ahead
questions.explain: Curve signs warn you of the direction of the road ahead; reduce speed before the curve.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 70)

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: This cross symbol warns that another road crosses yours ahead; watch for cross traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 70)

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road you are on ends ahead; you must turn left or right
A side road enters from the right
A dead-end alley on the left
The road divides into two lanes
questions.explain: A T-intersection sign warns that your road ends at a crossing road and a turn will be required.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 70)

questions.q: What should you be ready to do when you see this sign?
options: Speed up to block merging traffic
Change lanes immediately to the left
Adjust speed so traffic entering from the right can merge safely
Stop and wait for all merging traffic
questions.explain: Merge signs warn that two streams of traffic will join; be ready to allow vehicles into your lane.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 72)

questions.q: What does this sign indicate on a multilane road?
options: The road narrows to one lane for both directions
The right lane ends ahead; be prepared to merge left
A new lane is added on the right
questions.explain: Lane-reduction signs warn that the number of lanes is decreasing; change lanes or let others merge.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 71)

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A divided highway begins ahead; keep to the right of the median
questions.explain: This sign is posted before a center strip begins separating opposing traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 72)

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A traffic signal ahead that may not yet be visible
questions.explain: Signal-ahead signs give early warning so you can begin slowing for an upcoming traffic light.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 69)

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road is slippery when wet; slow down in wet weather
questions.explain: This sign warns of pavement that can make you lose control when wet; it takes longer to stop.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 70)

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Reduce speed before starting down a steep or long downgrade
Speed up to climb the hill
Shift to neutral to save fuel
questions.explain: The downgrade sign warns of a dangerous hill; slow down before you begin the descent.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 71)

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: A school zone with a 20 mph limit
A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead; watch for people crossing
Pedestrians are not allowed on this road
questions.explain: Pedestrian crossing signs warn of crosswalks, which are not always at intersections.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 68)

questions.q: This five-sided sign means what?
options: A school zone or school crossing is near; watch for children
A playground with no speed limit
questions.explain: Pentagon-shaped signs mark school zones and school crossings.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Shapes of Signs' (p. 64)

questions.q: What does this round yellow sign mean?
options: A railroad crossing is ahead; slow down, look and listen
You must stop at the sign
A railroad runs parallel to the road
questions.explain: This advance warning sign may be up to 750 feet before the crossing in rural areas.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Shapes of Signs' (p. 63)

questions.q: This pennant-shaped sign is posted on the left side of a two-lane road. What does it mean?
questions.explain: The yellow pennant marks the start of a no-passing zone on two-lane, two-way roads.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Shapes of Signs' (p. 64)

questions.q: This small plaque is mounted under a curve warning sign. What does it tell you?
options: The posted speed limit for the whole highway
The advised maximum safe speed for the curve
The distance to the curve in feet
The minimum speed on the curve
questions.explain: A speed plaque below a curve or turn arrow shows the maximum safe speed for that curve.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 70)

questions.q: What does an orange diamond sign like this mean?
options: There is construction or maintenance work ahead; slow down and be alert
questions.explain: Orange warning signs mark construction and maintenance zones; obey the work-zone speed limit.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Construction and Maintenance Signs' (p. 72)

questions.q: What should you do after seeing this sign?
options: Slow down and be ready to obey a flagger's signals, including stopping
Proceed at normal speed since flaggers only direct trucks
questions.explain: This sign warns of a flagger ahead; you must stop if signaled to do so.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Construction and Maintenance Signs' (p. 73)

questions.q: You are behind a vehicle displaying this emblem. What does it mean?
options: The vehicle moves slowly; slow down and pass only when safe and legal
The vehicle is about to turn left
The vehicle is a school bus
The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials
questions.explain: The orange triangle marks slow-moving vehicles, which usually travel 5–20 mph.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Other Special Signs' (p. 74)

questions.q: You are stopped at this signal and want to turn right. What does Illinois law allow?
options: Never turn until the light turns green
Turn right only if a police officer waves you through
Turn right without stopping if no one is coming
After a complete stop, turn right after yielding to pedestrians and traffic unless a sign forbids it
questions.explain: Illinois allows a right turn on red after a full stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals' (p. 77)

questions.q: What must you do when you approach this signal?
options: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe
Stop and wait until it turns green
Speed up to clear the intersection
Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping
questions.explain: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals' (p. 77)

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: The signal is broken; treat it as an all-way stop
Pedestrians have the right of way only
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light means you may proceed into the intersection with caution.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals' (p. 77)

questions.q: What does this green arrow allow?
options: A left turn in the direction of the arrow, after yielding to anyone still in the intersection or crosswalk
A left turn only after stopping first
questions.explain: A green arrow allows the movement shown once you yield to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals' (p. 78)

questions.q: With a solid and a broken yellow line between opposing lanes, when may you pass?
options: Only when the solid line is on your side
Only when the broken line is on your side
questions.explain: Passing is allowed only from the side next to the broken yellow line; the solid line on the other side means no passing.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings' (p. 80)

questions.q: Two solid yellow center lines separate opposing traffic. When may you cross them?
options: Only to turn left into or out of an alley, driveway, private road or street
To pass a slow vehicle when the road is clear
questions.explain: Double solid yellow lines mark the center of the road and may be crossed only to turn left.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings' (p. 79)

questions.q: What is the center lane marked like this used for?
options: Left turns (and legal U-turns) by traffic from either direction
questions.explain: A two-way left turn lane may be used only to prepare for or make a left turn or permitted U-turn.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings' (p. 80)

questions.q: What do broken white lines like these separate?
options: A bike lane from a parking lane
Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction
questions.explain: Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes; cross them only to change lanes or turn.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings' (p. 79)

questions.q: What does an eight-sided (octagon) sign always mean?
questions.explain: Only stop signs use the octagon shape.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Shapes of Signs' (p. 63)

questions.q: What color are signs used in construction and maintenance work zones?
questions.explain: Orange warning signs alert you to construction and maintenance work.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Colors of Signs' (p. 64)

questions.q: Fluorescent yellow-green warning signs are used mainly for what?
options: Pedestrian, bicycle, school and playground crossings
questions.explain: Yellow-green signs mark pedestrian and bicycle crossings, playgrounds, school bus stops and school zones.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Colors of Signs' (p. 64)

questions.q: You face a steady red arrow pointing right. Under Illinois law you may:
options: Never turn until a green arrow appears
Turn right after stopping completely and yielding to traffic and pedestrians
questions.explain: Illinois allows a right turn on a red arrow after a full stop and yielding.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals' (p. 78)

questions.q: A traffic signal at an intersection is not working at all. What should you do?
options: Follow the vehicle in front through the intersection
Treat it as an all-way stop: stop, then yield before entering
Treat it as a yield sign
questions.explain: When signals are out, treat the intersection as an all-way stop unless an officer directs otherwise.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals' (p. 77)

questions.q: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time on different roads. Who should go first?
questions.explain: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: At a four-way stop, three vehicles stop at different times. Which goes first?
options: The vehicle on the far right
questions.explain: At an all-way stop, the first driver to stop is the first to go.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: At an uncontrolled intersection, two vehicles on different roads arrive at the same time. What is the rule?
options: The driver on the right yields to the driver on the left
Both must stop and wait for a signal
The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right
questions.explain: With no signs or signals, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: You are on the road that ends at a T-intersection with no signs or signals. Who has the right of way?
options: Traffic on the through road; you must yield
You do, because you are turning
questions.explain: The driver on the terminating road of a T-intersection must yield to cross traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: You are turning left at a green light. Whom must you yield to?
options: Oncoming traffic and pedestrians in the crosswalk
No one, because the light is green
questions.explain: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: You entered an intersection on green to turn left and the light turns red while you wait for oncoming traffic. What should you do?
options: Stay in the intersection until the next green
Complete the turn when oncoming traffic clears
Back up out of the intersection
questions.explain: If you entered while the light was green, you may finish the turn even after it turns red.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: Your light turns green, but a car is still crossing the intersection. What must you do?
options: Wait and yield to vehicles still in the intersection
Go immediately because you have the green
questions.explain: You must yield to vehicles in the intersection even after your light turns green.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: You are leaving a private driveway in a city to enter the street. What is required?
options: Stop before the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians and all vehicles
Stop only if a pedestrian is visible
Slow down and enter if the street looks clear
questions.explain: In urban areas you must stop before the sidewalk when leaving an alley, building, private road or driveway, then yield.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 34)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights approaches you from behind. What does Illinois law require?
options: Pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop if needed until it passes
Speed up to stay ahead of it
questions.explain: Drivers must immediately pull to the right and allow the emergency vehicle to pass, stopping if necessary.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 25)

questions.q: You are approaching a police car stopped on the shoulder with its emergency lights flashing. What does Illinois law require?
options: Change to a lane away from it if possible, slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explain: For stationary emergency or maintenance vehicles with flashing lights, move away when possible, reduce speed and use caution.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 25)

questions.q: Within what distance of an emergency scene does Illinois law generally prohibit using a phone or taking photos while driving?
questions.explain: Illinois bans phone use and taking photos while driving within 500 feet of an emergency scene, with limited exceptions.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 25)

questions.q: You meet a funeral procession at an intersection. What should you do?
options: Join the procession to get through
Cut through gaps between procession vehicles
Proceed if your light is green
Yield to all vehicles in the procession
questions.explain: Drivers must yield to all vehicles in a funeral procession and must not drive between them.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 26)

questions.q: A pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk ahead of you. What must you do?
options: Proceed if they are not in your lane
Stop and yield to the pedestrian
Slow down and drive around them
questions.explain: Drivers must stop and yield when a pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 27)

questions.q: There is no traffic signal, and a pedestrian is crossing in an unmarked crosswalk on your side of the road. What must you do?
options: Continue, because the crosswalk is not marked
Only yield if the pedestrian is a child
questions.explain: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in an unmarked crosswalk on the driver's side of the road when there are no signals.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 27)

questions.q: A pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is crossing the street. What is your duty?
options: Proceed if the pedestrian is outside a crosswalk
questions.explain: Pedestrians with disabilities using a white cane, guide dog or other aid have the right of way.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Pedestrians' (p. 40)

questions.q: A pedestrian started crossing before your light turned green. What should you do?
options: Go, because your light is green
questions.explain: You must yield to a pedestrian who entered the crosswalk before the light changed.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 27)

questions.q: When entering a roundabout, whom must you yield to?
options: No one; entering traffic has priority
All traffic already in the roundabout, plus pedestrians and bicyclists
questions.explain: Vehicles entering or exiting a roundabout must yield to all traffic, pedestrians and bicycles.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Rotary and Roundabout' (p. 32)

questions.q: In which direction does traffic travel in an Illinois roundabout?
options: Whichever way the first driver chooses
questions.explain: Traffic circulates counterclockwise around the central island; you enter by turning right.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Rotary and Roundabout' (p. 32)

questions.q: You are turning on a flashing yellow left-turn arrow. What must you do?
options: Turn only if no one is behind you
Turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Stop and wait for the arrow to turn green
Turn immediately; you have a protected turn
questions.explain: A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn only after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming vehicles.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Traffic Signals' (p. 78)

questions.q: You may not enter an intersection or marked crosswalk unless:
options: There is enough room on the other side for your vehicle
questions.explain: Do not enter an intersection or crosswalk unless there is space to clear it without blocking others.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: You approach a disabled vehicle with its hazard lights flashing on a four-lane highway. What does Illinois law require?
options: Change lanes away from it if safe; otherwise slow down while passing
questions.explain: Drivers must move away from a disabled vehicle using hazard lights when it is safe, or reduce speed when passing it.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Disabled Vehicles' (p. 45)

questions.q: On a highway with a YIELD sign at an entrance ramp, what is your responsibility?
options: Merge at your current speed regardless of gaps
Stop at the sign every time
Adjust speed and let through traffic go before you merge
Through traffic must make room for you
questions.explain: At a yield or merge, you must slow or stop as needed to avoid a crash with through traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 65)

questions.q: When does a pedestrian crossing in the middle of a block (not at a crosswalk) have to yield?
options: Always: pedestrians outside a crosswalk must yield to vehicles
Never: pedestrians always have the right of way
questions.explain: Pedestrians crossing anywhere other than a marked or unmarked crosswalk must give the right of way to drivers, though drivers should still be prepared to stop.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Pedestrians' (p. 40)

questions.q: On school days, when must you stop and yield at a school zone crosswalk?
options: Never, if the signal is green
Only when a crossing guard is present
When children or adults are in or near the crosswalk
questions.explain: In a school zone you must stop and yield to children or adults in the crosswalk area.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 26)

questions.q: Unless another limit is posted, what is the speed limit on Illinois interstates and tollways?
questions.explain: Interstates and tollways have a 70 mph limit unless otherwise posted.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on an Illinois four-lane highway?
questions.explain: Four-lane highways have a 65 mph limit unless otherwise posted.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on other highways and in rural areas?
questions.explain: Other highways and rural areas are limited to 55 mph unless otherwise posted.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in Illinois cities and towns?
questions.explain: The default limit in city and town areas is 30 mph.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: What is the speed limit in an alley in Illinois?
questions.explain: Alleys have a 15 mph limit unless otherwise posted.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: What is the school zone speed limit in Illinois when children are present and signs are posted?
questions.explain: In a posted school zone the limit is 20 mph on school days when children are present.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: During what hours does the 20 mph school zone limit apply on school days?
options: 6:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., when children are present
7 a.m. to 3 p.m. at all times
questions.explain: The reduced school speed applies on school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: When does a posted construction zone speed limit apply?
options: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, whether or not workers are present
questions.explain: Construction zone speed limits must be obeyed at all times, regardless of the presence of workers.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 25)

questions.q: A second conviction for speeding in a construction zone with workers present within two years results in what?
options: A smaller fine than the first
questions.explain: A second work-zone speeding violation within two years when workers are present leads to suspension.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 8 Revocation, Suspension, Denial and Cancellation, 'Suspension' (p. 60)

questions.q: What is the 'three-second rule' used for?
options: Judging a safe following distance behind the vehicle ahead
Measuring how long to look in mirrors
Timing a stop at a stop sign
questions.explain: Pick a fixed object; if you reach it before counting three seconds after the car ahead passes it, you are too close.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Following Distances' (p. 83)

questions.q: According to the handbook, what causes most rear-end crashes?
questions.explain: Tailgating is the cause of most rear-end crashes.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Following Distances' (p. 83)

questions.q: When roads are wet or weather is poor, how should you change your following distance?
options: Following distance does not depend on weather
questions.explain: The three-second rule is for good roads and weather; increase the distance when conditions are poor.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Following Distances' (p. 83)

questions.q: If you double your speed, what happens to your stopping distance?
options: It becomes about four times as long
questions.explain: Doubling speed quadruples the stopping distance.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Vehicle Speed' (p. 84)

questions.q: At 55 mph, about how many feet does a vehicle travel in one second?
questions.explain: At 55 mph a vehicle covers about 81 feet each second, so three seconds is about 243 feet.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Following Distances' (p. 83)

questions.q: Using the three-second rule at 70 mph, about how far back should you be from the vehicle ahead?
questions.explain: At 70 mph a car travels about 103 feet per second, so three seconds is roughly 309 feet.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Following Distances' (p. 83)

questions.q: If no minimum speed is posted, how slowly may you drive?
options: Not so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic
No slower than half the speed limit
questions.explain: Even without a posted minimum, you must not drive so slowly that you interfere with normal traffic movement.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: When must you slow down below the posted limit?
options: When approaching intersections, curves or hilltops, or on narrow winding roads and in poor weather
Never, if the limit is posted
Only when a police officer is present
questions.explain: You must slow when approaching and crossing intersections, curves and hills and when conditions are unfavorable.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Speed Limits' (p. 24)

questions.q: What is the maximum speed of a low-speed vehicle, and on what streets may it be driven?
options: 35 mph, on any road except interstates
25 mph maximum, on streets posted 30 mph or less unless locally prohibited
questions.explain: Low-speed vehicles are capped at 25 mph and may use streets posted 30 mph or less.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Low-Speed Vehicles' (p. 46)

questions.q: When you are being tailgated, what is the best response?
options: Move to another lane or pull over safely and let the driver pass
questions.explain: Let the tailgater pass by changing lanes or pulling off; slamming on the brakes is aggressive driving.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Following Distances' (p. 83)

questions.q: On a freeway, what do signs showing both a maximum and a minimum speed mean?
options: The minimum is only a suggestion
You may exceed the maximum to pass
Driving below the minimum is illegal unless necessary for safety
questions.explain: Driving slower than a posted minimum speed is illegal unless needed for safety.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Regulatory Signs' (p. 66)

questions.q: In thick fog, what does the handbook advise?
options: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed
Use high beams to see farther
Slow down, use low beams or fog lights, and pull off the road if the fog is too dense
Follow the tail lights ahead closely
questions.explain: In fog, slow down, use dim lights or fog lights, don't overdrive your lights, and pull off and stop if it is too dense.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Weather Conditions' (p. 84)

questions.q: When leaving a construction zone, when may you resume normal speed?
options: Once you are safely past any workers or work vehicles
As soon as the first orange sign is behind you
questions.explain: Keep a reduced speed until you are safely past workers and authorized vehicles.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 25)

questions.q: In a business or residential district, how far before turning must you begin signaling?
questions.explain: Signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning in business or residential areas.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Signaling' (p. 30)

questions.q: Outside business and residential districts, how far ahead must you signal a turn?
questions.explain: Outside business and residential districts, start a continuous signal no less than 200 feet before the turn.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Signaling' (p. 30)

questions.q: What is the hand signal for a right turn?
options: Right arm out the passenger window
questions.explain: For a right turn, extend the left hand and arm straight up.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Signaling' (p. 30)

questions.q: What is the hand signal for slowing down or stopping?
questions.explain: To slow or stop, extend the left hand and arm down.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Signaling' (p. 30)

questions.q: What is the hand signal for a left turn?
options: Left arm extended straight out to the side
questions.explain: For a left turn, extend the left hand and arm straight out.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Signaling' (p. 30)

questions.q: When making a right turn, where should your vehicle end up?
options: In the left lane of the new road
In the right-hand lane of the road you enter, staying close to the curb
In any lane of the new road
questions.explain: Follow the curb closely and turn into the right-hand lane.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Turning' (p. 31)

questions.q: When making a left turn, which lane should you turn into?
options: The lane closest to your direction of travel
questions.explain: Complete a left turn into the lane closest to the intended direction.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Turning' (p. 31)

questions.q: While waiting to turn left, where should your front wheels point?
options: Straight ahead until you begin the turn
questions.explain: Keep wheels straight so that if you are hit from behind you are not pushed into oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Turning' (p. 31)

questions.q: When may you turn left on a red light in Illinois?
options: From a one-way street onto another one-way street with traffic moving left, after a full stop and yielding
Only when a green arrow shows
From any street after a full stop
questions.explain: Left on red is allowed only from one-way to one-way (traffic moving left) after stopping and yielding.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Right of Way' (p. 26)

questions.q: Unless you can see at least how far in every direction, you may not make a U-turn on a curve or hill?
questions.explain: U-turns on curves and hills are banned unless you can see at least 500 feet in all directions.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Turning' (p. 32)

questions.q: When passing on a two-lane road, you must return to your lane before coming within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle?
questions.explain: You must be back in your lane before getting within 200 feet of oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 28)

questions.q: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: As soon as your front bumper clears theirs
When you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror
When the other driver flashes their lights
questions.explain: Do not return until the whole passed vehicle is visible in the rearview mirror.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 28)

questions.q: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road is prohibited within how many feet of an intersection or railroad crossing?
questions.explain: No passing within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 29)

questions.q: Is passing allowed in Illinois construction zones?
options: Yes, if the speed limit is above 45 mph
Yes, if no workers are present
No; all Illinois construction zones are no-passing zones
questions.explain: All construction zones in Illinois are no-passing zones.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 29)

questions.q: What must the driver of a vehicle being passed do?
options: Not increase speed until the pass is complete
Flash the turn signal to wave them by
questions.explain: The driver being passed must not speed up until the other driver has completed the pass.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 28)

questions.q: Is it legal to flash your turn signal to tell the driver behind it's safe to pass?
options: Yes, it's required on two-lane roads
No, using turn signals as a courtesy 'do pass' signal is illegal
questions.explain: Illinois prohibits flashing turn signals as a courtesy pass signal.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 28)

questions.q: When may you pass another vehicle on the right?
options: When it is turning left and there is room, or on a one-way street or road with two or more lanes each way
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed in limited situations and never by driving on the shoulder.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 28)

questions.q: May you drive on the shoulder to pass a vehicle turning left?
options: Yes, if the shoulder is paved
No, driving off the pavement to pass is not allowed
questions.explain: Leaving the pavement or main traveled part of the road to pass is prohibited.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 28)

questions.q: On an Illinois interstate, when may you drive in the left lane?
options: Mainly when passing, or in exceptions such as congestion, weather, hazards, or moving over for emergency vehicles
Any time, as long as you signal
Whenever you are going the speed limit
questions.explain: On interstates and controlled freeways the left lane is for passing, with a few listed exceptions.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Lane Usage' (p. 29)

questions.q: When a two-way left turn lane is provided in the center of a road, how must left turns be made?
options: From the two-way left turn lane only
questions.explain: Where a center two-way left turn lane exists, left turns must be made from it and not from another lane.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings' (p. 80)

questions.q: Before changing lanes, what should you do besides checking mirrors?
options: Turn your head to check the blind spot, then signal
questions.explain: Check behind and to the side by turning your head, and signal before moving over.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Turning' (p. 31)

questions.q: When a lane closes in heavy, slow-moving traffic, what does the handbook recommend?
options: Stop in the closing lane until someone waves you in
Use both lanes up to the merge point, then take turns merging ('zipper merge')
Use the shoulder to get ahead
Merge as early as possible no matter what
questions.explain: In congestion, use both lanes to the lane-reduction point and alternate; merge early when traffic is light.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Warning Signs' (p. 71)

questions.q: What should you do when you leave a roundabout?
questions.explain: Signal right to show other drivers you are exiting the roundabout.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Rotary and Roundabout' (p. 32)

questions.q: You missed your exit on the expressway. What should you do?
options: Make a U-turn through the median
Stop and wait for a gap to reverse
questions.explain: Backing up on an expressway is illegal; go to the next exit.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 86)

questions.q: How should you enter an expressway from an entrance ramp?
options: Use the speed-change lane to match traffic speed, signal and merge into a safe gap
Enter slowly so traffic notices you
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait
questions.explain: Use the acceleration lane to reach traffic speed, then merge when it is safe.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 86)

questions.q: May you drive across an unpaved median strip or a median barrier to change direction?
options: No, it is unlawful to drive across median strips or barriers
questions.explain: Crossing unpaved median strips or median barriers is illegal; only a paved dividing space may be crossed to turn left, and only if no sign or signal prohibits it.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Lane Usage' (p. 29)

questions.q: When a solid yellow no-passing line is on your side of the center line, when may you cross it?
options: To finish a pass begun before the zone started, or to turn left into or out of a driveway or alley
To pass a slow vehicle when the road is clear
questions.explain: You may cross it only to complete a pass already started before the zone, or to turn left into or from an alley, private road or driveway.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Pavement Markings' (p. 79)

questions.q: You park downhill on a street with a curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
questions.explain: Downhill with a curb, turn wheels toward the curb so the car will roll into it.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 34)

questions.q: You park uphill on a street with a curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: Toward the curb, with the parking brake off
questions.explain: Uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 34)

questions.q: You park on a hill on a road with no curb. How should your front wheels be turned?
options: Toward the center of the road
Toward the side of the road where you are parked (to the right)
questions.explain: Without a curb, turn the wheels toward the side of the road so the car rolls away from traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 34)

questions.q: When parallel parking on a two-way street, how close to the curb must your right wheels be?
questions.explain: Park with right-hand wheels parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 35)

questions.q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Illinois?
questions.explain: Standing or parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 35)

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
questions.explain: Standing or parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection is prohibited.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 36)

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal?
questions.explain: Do not stand or park closer than 30 feet to a STOP sign, YIELD sign or traffic signal.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 36)

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Parking is not allowed closer than 50 feet to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 36)

questions.q: How close to a fire station driveway may you park?
questions.explain: Parking within 20 feet of a fire station driveway is prohibited.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 36)

questions.q: Where is stopping, standing or parking prohibited?
options: Next to a curb painted white
On a bridge, sidewalk, crosswalk or within an intersection
questions.explain: Statewide rules prohibit stopping on bridges, sidewalks, crosswalks, intersections, railroad tracks and in tunnels.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 35)

questions.q: May you park in a marked or protected bike lane for a quick stop?
options: Yes, if no bicyclists are visible
Yes, for up to five minutes
No, stopping, standing or parking in a bike lane is prohibited
questions.explain: Vehicles may not park, idle, or drop off passengers in bike lanes, even when no bicyclists are present.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 35)

questions.q: Outside a business or residential district, if you must stop on the paved road in an emergency, how much clear view is needed?
questions.explain: In an emergency you may stop only where there is a clear view of 200 feet in each direction; use your flashers.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Prohibited Stopping, Standing or Parking' (p. 36)

questions.q: Can a vehicle with a disability placard park in the striped area next to an accessible space?
options: No, the striped access aisle is part of the space and may not be parked in
Yes, if the placard is permanent
Yes, if the accessible space is full
questions.explain: Even with a placard or plates, vehicles may not park in the striped area beside an accessible space.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 35)

questions.q: When parking on a hill, what should you do in addition to turning the wheels correctly?
options: Put the vehicle in park and set the parking brake
questions.explain: On a hill, shift into park and use the parking brake as needed, along with turning the wheels the correct way.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 34)

questions.q: When parking on a street, which direction must your vehicle face?
options: The direction traffic is moving in that lane
Against traffic so you can see oncoming cars
questions.explain: Parked vehicles must face the same way that traffic moves on that side of the street.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 35)

questions.q: Who may use a parking space reserved for electric vehicle charging?
options: Any vehicle for up to one hour
questions.explain: Only electric vehicles may park in designated charging spaces.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Parking' (p. 35)

questions.q: On a two-lane road, a school bus stops ahead of you with red lights flashing and stop arm out. What must you do?
options: Stop, then proceed after five seconds
Stop and stay stopped until the arm is withdrawn and lights stop flashing, or the driver signals you to go
Pass on the left if no children are visible
Slow to 10 mph and pass carefully
questions.explain: You must stop before meeting or overtaking a stopped school bus loading or unloading passengers.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 33)

questions.q: When are you NOT required to stop for a stopped school bus with its stop arm out?
options: When you are on a four-lane roadway and the bus is stopped in the opposite direction
When you are behind the bus on a two-lane road
When the bus is in a school parking lot
questions.explain: The only exception is a four-lane road with the bus stopped for opposite-direction traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 32)

questions.q: Do Illinois school bus stopping rules apply in a parking lot on school property?
questions.explain: Drivers must stop for a stopped school bus on any roadway, private road, or school parking lot.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 33)

questions.q: How far in advance of a stop does a school bus give warning in a rural area?
questions.explain: School buses warn at least 100 feet before a stop, or 200 feet in rural areas.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 33)

questions.q: What is the penalty for a conviction of passing a stopped school bus that has its stop arm extended?
options: License suspension, a $300 mandatory fine and community service
questions.explain: The conviction results in a driver's license suspension, a mandatory $300 fine and court-ordered community service.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 33)

questions.q: When passing a bicyclist, what is the minimum distance Illinois requires between your vehicle and the bicycle?
questions.explain: Leave at least 3 feet when passing a bicyclist, including one in a bike lane or on the shoulder.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles' (p. 43)

questions.q: When passing a pedestrian walking on the road or shoulder, what minimum clearance must you give?
questions.explain: Keep at least 3 feet between your vehicle and a pedestrian when passing.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Passing' (p. 28)

questions.q: You are turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on your right. What should you do?
options: Let the bicyclist go through the intersection first, then turn
Turn quickly ahead of the bicyclist
questions.explain: Let the bicyclist pass through the intersection before you turn right.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles' (p. 43)

questions.q: What is the 'Dutch Reach'?
options: Opening your car door with the hand farthest from it, so you turn and look for bicyclists
Reaching for your seat belt before starting
questions.explain: Using your right hand to open the driver's door turns your body so you can see bicyclists and traffic behind.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles' (p. 43)

questions.q: How many bicyclists may ride side by side on an Illinois roadway?
options: Two, if they do not impede normal traffic
questions.explain: Bicyclists may ride two abreast if traffic is not impeded; more than two is prohibited except on bike paths.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles' (p. 43)

questions.q: Why should you not share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: Motorcycles must ride on the shoulder
It is allowed if you stay to the right
The motorcyclist is entitled to the full lane and needs room to maneuver
questions.explain: Motorcyclists are entitled to the entire lane; do not share it.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles' (p. 41)

questions.q: Where do more than half of all motorcycle crashes happen?
options: At intersections, often when a car turns left in front of a motorcycle
questions.explain: Over 50% of motorcycle crashes occur at intersections; the most common is an oncoming car turning left.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles' (p. 41)

questions.q: What following distance does the handbook recommend behind a motorcycle?
options: At least three to four seconds
Same as behind a car: one car length
questions.explain: Allow at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has room to maneuver.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles' (p. 42)

questions.q: Under Illinois law, after how long may a motorcyclist proceed through a red light that fails to change?
options: 120 seconds, after yielding to other traffic
questions.explain: If a red light does not turn green after 120 seconds, a motorcyclist may proceed after yielding.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles' (p. 41)

questions.q: Why should you dim your headlights when following a truck at night?
options: Bright lights reflect off the truck's large mirrors and blind the driver
Trucks have sensors that react to bright light
It is only required in cities
questions.explain: High beams reflect in a truck's large side mirrors and blind its driver.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Large Vehicles' (p. 45)

questions.q: A large truck ahead signals a right turn and swings left first. What should you do?
options: Honk and pass on the left
Stay back and do not move into the space on its right
questions.explain: Large vehicles make wide right turns and may leave space on the right; give them room.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Large Vehicles' (p. 45)

questions.q: What are a large truck's 'No Zones'?
options: Blind spots around the truck where its driver cannot see you
Zones where passing trucks is illegal
Areas where trucks may not park
questions.explain: Stay out of blind spots and keep a position where the truck driver can see you in the mirrors.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Large Vehicles' (p. 45)

questions.q: How fast do slow-moving vehicles such as farm equipment usually travel?
questions.explain: Normal speeds for slow-moving vehicles range from 5 to 20 mph, so you close on them very quickly.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Slow-Moving Vehicles' (p. 46)

questions.q: What should you avoid doing near a horseback rider?
questions.explain: Never sound a horn near horses or livestock; it may frighten them and cause a crash.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Horseback Riders' (p. 47)

questions.q: When there is no sidewalk, where should pedestrians walk on a two-way road?
options: Facing oncoming traffic, keeping as far from moving vehicles as possible
In the center of the lane
questions.explain: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic, on the shoulder when there is one, staying as far from traffic as possible.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Pedestrians' (p. 40)

questions.q: Who may operate a Class 3 low-speed electric bicycle in Illinois?
options: Only licensed drivers age 18 or older
questions.explain: Class 3 e-bikes, which assist up to 28 mph, may be operated only by riders 16 or older.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles' (p. 44)

questions.q: What license is required to operate a moped in Illinois?
questions.explain: A moped (no gear shifting, combustion engine 50cc or less) may be operated with any valid driver's license.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Scooters and Mopeds' (p. 44)

questions.q: A scooter with an engine smaller than 150cc is a motor-driven cycle. What license does it require?
questions.explain: Scooters under 150cc require a Class L license; 150cc or more requires Class M.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Scooters and Mopeds' (p. 44)

questions.q: On which roads are bicyclists prohibited?
options: Any road with a center line
questions.explain: Bicycles are not allowed on controlled-access highways, expressways and other roads marked to exclude them.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles' (p. 42)

questions.q: You are turning left and a bicyclist is coming through the intersection from the opposite direction. What should you do?
options: Turn if the bicyclist is in a bike lane
Turn first since cars have priority
Wait for the bicyclist to pass before turning
questions.explain: Wait for an oncoming bicyclist to pass before making a left turn, just as you would for a car.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Bicycles' (p. 43)

questions.q: Why are motorcycles often involved in crashes with cars?
options: Drivers fail to see them and underestimate their speed
questions.explain: Failure to detect and recognize motorcycles is the most common cause; their small size makes speed hard to judge.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Motorcycles' (p. 41)

questions.q: Who may skate on Illinois public roadways, and where?
options: No one; skating on roads is illegal
Only children under 12, on residential streets
People 18 or older, on roads posted 45 mph or less, from sunrise to sunset, if traffic is not impeded
questions.explain: Pedestrians 18+ may skate on roads posted 45 mph or less between sunrise and sunset without impeding traffic.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Pedestrians' (p. 40)

questions.q: Under Illinois law, which drivers may use a hands-free phone while driving?
questions.explain: Handheld use is banned for everyone; hands-free or Bluetooth is allowed only for drivers 19 and older.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Distracted Driving' (p. 22)

questions.q: Which of these is a legal time for an adult to use a handheld phone in a vehicle?
options: While parked on the shoulder of the road
While using speakerphone in your hand
While stopped at a red light in drive
questions.explain: Handheld use is allowed only to report an emergency, while parked on the shoulder, or when stopped in obstructed traffic in neutral or park.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Distracted Driving' (p. 22)

questions.q: Is holding your phone and talking on speakerphone while driving legal in Illinois?
options: No, it is not considered hands-free
Yes, speakerphone always counts as hands-free
questions.explain: Holding the phone while using speakerphone is a violation of Illinois law.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Distracted Driving' (p. 22)

questions.q: Which of these is illegal on a phone while driving in Illinois?
options: Watching a live video, joining a video conference, or using social media
Using voice commands with a mounted phone (age 19+)
Using a single-sided earpiece for a call (age 19+)
questions.explain: Streaming live video, video conferencing and accessing social media while driving are violations.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Distracted Driving' (p. 22)

questions.q: What does Illinois law say about wearing headsets while driving?
options: Headsets are prohibited, but a single-sided earpiece for a phone is allowed
Headsets covering both ears are allowed
Any headphones are allowed at low volume
questions.explain: Headsets are prohibited while driving; a single-sided headset or earpiece is permitted.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Distracted Driving' (p. 22)

questions.q: Who must wear a seat belt in Illinois?
options: The driver and all passengers age 8 and older, front and back seats
Only passengers in vehicles without air bags
questions.explain: Illinois requires safety belts for all drivers and passengers 8 and older in every seat, even with air bags.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Safety Belt Law' (p. 23)

questions.q: Who is responsible for making sure all passengers obey the seat belt and child restraint laws?
options: The vehicle owner, even if not present
questions.explain: It is the driver's responsibility to ensure all passengers follow the belt law and Child Passenger Protection Act.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Safety Belt Law' (p. 23)

questions.q: Under the Child Passenger Protection Act, children under what age must be secured in an appropriate child restraint system?
questions.explain: The Child Passenger Protection Act requires every child under 8 to ride in a suitable child restraint, such as a car seat or booster.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Child Passenger Protection Act' (p. 23)

questions.q: Until what age must Illinois children ride rear-facing (unless they weigh more than 40 lb or are taller than 40 in)?
questions.explain: Since 2019, children must ride rear-facing until 2 unless over 40 pounds or 40 inches.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Child Passenger Protection Act' (p. 24)

questions.q: Where should a lap belt be worn?
questions.explain: The lap belt goes across the hip bones, never across the soft abdomen; the shoulder strap must not go behind the back or under the arm.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Safety Belt Law' (p. 23)

questions.q: What distance between the driver's chest and the steering-wheel air bag is recommended?
questions.explain: A distance of 10–12 inches from the air bag is desirable.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Safety Belt Law' (p. 23)

questions.q: When must headlights be on in Illinois?
options: From sunset to sunrise and whenever weather requires windshield wipers
questions.explain: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and when rain, snow or fog requires wipers.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: When must you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle?
questions.explain: Dim high beams 500 feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 87)

questions.q: When following another vehicle at night, how close may you get before dimming your high beams?
questions.explain: Dim high beams 300 feet before passing (approaching from behind) another vehicle.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 87)

questions.q: Headlights should also be used when you cannot see objects at what distance?
questions.explain: Use headlights when objects 1,000 feet away cannot be seen.
