questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: Your car starts to hydroplane on a wet road. What should you do?
options: Ease off the accelerator and avoid hard braking
questions.explain: Slow down to avoid hydroplaning; if it happens, release the accelerator and ride it out rather than braking quickly.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Weather Conditions' (p. 85)

questions.q: Your vehicle begins to skid. What does the handbook advise?
options: Brake hard and steer the opposite way
Ease off the gas or brake and steer in the direction of the skid, then straighten
questions.explain: Ease off the pedal and steer into the direction of the skid until you regain traction.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 87)

questions.q: Your right wheels drift off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?
options: Speed up and steer left sharply
Jerk the wheel back onto the pavement
Grip the wheel, ease off the gas, brake gently, then steer back on gently after checking traffic
questions.explain: Jerking the wheel can send you into oncoming traffic; slow gently and ease back on.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 87)

questions.q: Which part of the road often stays icy after the rest of the road is clear?
questions.explain: Bridges, overpasses and shaded areas may remain icy after other pavement is dry.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Weather Conditions' (p. 85)

questions.q: You come to a flooded road or viaduct. What should you do?
options: Drive through quickly to avoid stalling
Turn around and find another route
questions.explain: Never drive through flooded areas; you cannot judge depth or current.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Weather Conditions' (p. 85)

questions.q: You are stranded in your vehicle during a blizzard. What should you do?
options: Run the engine continuously with windows closed
Leave the vehicle and wait outside
Stay in the vehicle, run the engine only briefly with a window slightly open, and keep the tailpipe clear
questions.explain: Remain in the vehicle and guard against carbon monoxide.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Weather Conditions' (p. 85)

questions.q: An aggressive driver is yelling and gesturing at you. What should you do?
options: Brake suddenly in front of them
Follow them to get their plate number closely
Avoid eye contact and do not engage
questions.explain: Do not retaliate or make eye contact; keep doors locked and leave room to pull away.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Aggressive Driving' (p. 89)

questions.q: A vehicle is approaching head-on in your lane. What should you do?
options: Slow down, pull to the right, and sound your horn
Swerve left into the oncoming lane
questions.explain: Slow, move to the right and use the horn.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 87)

questions.q: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights or a lowered gate, where must you stop?
options: Anywhere you can see the train
Right at the edge of the tracks
Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail
questions.explain: Stop within 15–50 feet of the crossing when signals flash, gates are down or a train is approaching.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 33)

questions.q: A train has just passed at a crossing with multiple tracks and the lights stop flashing. What should you do?
options: Check for a second train on another track before crossing
questions.explain: Always look for another train on another track before proceeding.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 34)

questions.q: Which vehicles are required by law to stop at most railroad crossings?
options: Vehicles carrying passengers for hire, school buses, and hazardous-materials vehicles
questions.explain: Be prepared to stop behind buses, school buses and hazmat vehicles at crossings.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 33)

questions.q: What should you do when approaching a highway work zone?
options: Pass slower vehicles before the lane closes
Slow down, stop handheld phone use, yield to workers and change lanes away from them if possible
Speed up to clear the zone quickly
questions.explain: In work zones Illinois requires you to slow down, discontinue phone use (hands-free excepted), yield and move away from workers.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Construction Zones, Emergency Vehicles...' (p. 25)

questions.q: At what blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) is it illegal for a driver age 21 or older to drive in Illinois?
questions.explain: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of .08% or more.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Blood-Alcohol Concentration (BAC)/Presence of Drugs' (p. 48)

questions.q: Can you be convicted of DUI with a BAC below 0.08%?
options: Only if you cause a crash
Yes, if your driving ability is impaired
Only if you are a commercial driver
questions.explain: You can be convicted of DUI at less than .08% if your driving is impaired.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Blood-Alcohol Concentration (BAC)/Presence of Drugs' (p. 48)

questions.q: A driver under 21 is found to have any trace of alcohol while driving. What is the minimum penalty?
options: A driver's license suspension of at least three months
questions.explain: Under zero tolerance, any trace of alcohol for drivers under 21 brings at least a three-month suspension.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Drivers Under Age 21' (p. 52)

questions.q: What is the minimum penalty for a driver under 21 convicted of DUI for the first time?
options: Revocation of driving privileges for at least two years
questions.explain: Under-21 drivers convicted of DUI face at least a two-year revocation for a first conviction.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Drivers Under Age 21' (p. 52)

questions.q: Under Illinois' implied consent law, what have you agreed to by driving on Illinois roads?
options: To let police search your home
To submit to breath, blood, urine or other tests for alcohol or drugs if lawfully requested
To pay any traffic fine without court
questions.explain: Driving in Illinois means you automatically consent to chemical testing to determine impairment.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 49)

questions.q: A first-time offender's chemical test shows a BAC of 0.08% or more. What is the statutory summary suspension?
questions.explain: A failed test (BAC .08%+ or THC over the limit) brings a six-month suspension.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 49)

questions.q: A first-time offender refuses chemical testing after a DUI arrest. How long is the suspension?
questions.explain: Refusing chemical testing results in a one-year suspension for a first offender.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 49)

questions.q: A second offender (within five years) refuses chemical testing. How long is the suspension?
questions.explain: Second offenders face three years for a refusal and one year for a failed test.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 49)

questions.q: After a DUI arrest, the temporary receipt the officer gives you lets you drive for how many days before the summary suspension begins?
options: 45 days (the suspension starts on the 46th day)
questions.explain: The receipt allows driving for 45 days; the statutory summary suspension begins on the 46th day.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: What is the minimum revocation for a first DUI conviction in Illinois (driver 21 or older)?
questions.explain: A first DUI conviction brings at least a one-year revocation.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: What is the minimum revocation for a second DUI conviction within 20 years?
questions.explain: A second conviction within 20 years brings at least a five-year revocation.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: What is the penalty for a fourth DUI conviction?
questions.explain: A fourth and subsequent DUI conviction results in lifetime revocation.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: A DUI with a BAC at or above what level may bring enhanced penalties?
questions.explain: A DUI with a BAC of .16% or more, or while transporting a child under 16, may carry enhanced penalties.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: What is the legal THC limit for drivers in Illinois?
options: Any amount is legal for adults over 21
5 nanograms or more per milliliter of whole blood (or 10 ng/mL of other bodily substance)
questions.explain: Driving with THC of 5 ng/mL+ in whole blood or 10 ng/mL+ in another bodily substance is illegal.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Blood-Alcohol Concentration (BAC)/Presence of Drugs' (p. 48)

questions.q: How must cannabis be transported in a vehicle in Illinois?
options: In a sealed, odor-proof, child-resistant container
questions.explain: Cannabis may only be transported in a sealed, odor-proof, child-resistant container, and no one may use it in the vehicle.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Medical and Recreational Cannabis (Marijuana)' (p. 48)

questions.q: What is the only thing that removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explain: Food, coffee and showers do not speed elimination; only time does.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Blood-Alcohol Concentration (BAC)/Presence of Drugs' (p. 48)

questions.q: Is it legal for a passenger to have an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of an ordinary car?
options: No, open alcohol in the passenger area is illegal
Yes, if it is beer or wine
Yes, if the driver is sober
Yes, if the passenger is over 21
questions.explain: It is illegal to drink in a vehicle or to have an opened container in the passenger area (limos, chartered buses and motor homes excepted).
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Related DUI Offenses' (p. 51)

questions.q: If you refuse chemical testing after a crash causing death or serious personal injury, what happens?
options: Your driving privileges are revoked for at least one year
questions.explain: Refusing testing after a crash with serious injury or death brings at least a one-year revocation.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: What may a first-time DUI offender get to drive during a statutory summary suspension?
options: A Monitoring Device Driving Permit with a breath alcohol ignition interlock device
A permit valid only on weekends
questions.explain: An MDDP requires a BAIID installed in the vehicle; it cannot be issued to anyone under 18.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: Which of these can lead to an Aggravated DUI charge?
options: Refusing a field sobriety test without a crash
Driving with an expired registration sticker
Committing DUI without a valid license or insurance
A first DUI with BAC of 0.08%
questions.explain: Aggravated DUI includes DUI causing injury or death, a third DUI, DUI in a school bus, or DUI without a valid license or insurance.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Related DUI Offenses' (p. 51)

questions.q: A person under 21 receives court supervision for possessing alcohol while an occupant of a vehicle. What happens to their license?
options: Nothing, since they were not driving
questions.explain: Court supervision for possession/consumption while in a vehicle brings a three-month suspension; a conviction brings at least six months.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 3 Drivers Under Age 21, 'Related Laws' (p. 20)

questions.q: After a DUI conviction, for how long must you file proof of financial responsibility (SR-22) insurance?
questions.explain: A DUI conviction requires filing Financial Responsibility Insurance for three years.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 50)

questions.q: How does Illinois classify DUI and how long does a conviction stay on your driving record?
options: As a violent crime; it stays on your record permanently
As a minor infraction; removed after court supervision
As a petty offense; it is removed after one year
As a civil violation; removed after five years
questions.explain: DUI is classified in Illinois as a violent crime and a conviction remains permanently on the record.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 49)

questions.q: Can over-the-counter medicines such as antihistamines or cold remedies impair driving?
options: No, only illegal drugs impair driving
Yes, many prescription and nonprescription drugs impair driving
questions.explain: Antihistamines, cold remedies, pain relievers and many other drugs can impair safe driving.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'Other Drugs' (p. 49)

questions.q: If you refuse a breath test and a blood test is needed, how much of its cost might you have to pay if found guilty of DUI?
questions.explain: You may be held financially liable up to $500 for blood test costs.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 6 Driving Under the Influence, 'DUI Laws' (p. 49)

questions.q: A crash report must be filed regardless of fault when the crash involves death, injury, or property damage over what amount (all vehicles insured)?
questions.explain: A report is required for death, injury or damage over $1,500 ($500 if any vehicle is uninsured).
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Crash Reports' (p. 54)

questions.q: If any vehicle in a crash is uninsured, a report is required when property damage exceeds what amount?
questions.explain: When a vehicle involved is uninsured, damage over $500 requires a report.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Crash Reports' (p. 54)

questions.q: According to the Rules of the Road, how soon after a crash must a driver report it?
questions.explain: The handbook states a driver has 30 minutes to report a crash.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Crash Reports' (p. 55)

questions.q: What is the maximum penalty for failing to report a vehicle crash?
options: A fine up to $2,500 and up to one year in jail
questions.explain: Failing to report a crash can bring a fine up to $2,500 and up to a year in jail.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Crash Reports' (p. 55)

questions.q: A crash happens in a rural area with no officer at the scene. Whom should you notify?
options: The Secretary of State the next week
The county sheriff or Illinois State Police
questions.explain: In rural areas, notify the county sheriff or Illinois State Police.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Crash Reports' (p. 55)

questions.q: You damage a parked car whose owner cannot be found. What should you do?
options: Leave, since no one was hurt
Report it only if damage is over $1,500
Stop, leave a note with your name, address, phone and plate number, notify police and file any required report
questions.explain: Leave your contact information on the vehicle, notify police and complete required reports.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Unattended Vehicles' (p. 55)

questions.q: What happens to a driver convicted of leaving the scene of a crash where someone was injured or killed?
options: The Secretary of State must revoke the license, and criminal charges apply
questions.explain: Leaving the scene of an injury or fatal crash requires revocation; property damage over $1,000 brings suspension.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Leaving the Scene of a Crash' (p. 55)

questions.q: What is the first thing to do if you are involved in or come upon a crash, if you are able?
options: Leave the area to avoid congestion
Stop in a safe, well-lit place that does not block traffic
Drive to the nearest police station
questions.explain: Stop safely, help the injured if needed, call 911 and warn other drivers with flashers or flares.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 7 Traffic Violations/Crashes, 'Traffic Violations/Crashes' (p. 54)

questions.q: Your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks and a train is coming. What should everyone do?
options: Get out immediately and move away from the tracks at an angle toward the train, then call 911
Stay in the vehicle with belts on
Stand beside the vehicle and wave to the train engineer
questions.explain: Move away at a 45-degree angle toward the train so debris does not hit you, and call 911.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Special Stops' (p. 33)

questions.q: Where can you find the phone number to report a problem at a railroad crossing?
options: On the blue Emergency Notification System sign posted at the crossing
On the round yellow advance sign
questions.explain: The blue ENS sign at the crossing lists the railroad's emergency number and a crossing ID.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 10 Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings, 'Railroad Crossings' (p. 81)

questions.q: You are pulled over by police. What should you do?
options: Get out and walk to the squad car
Search the glove box right away
Keep driving until you reach home
Stay in the vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel
questions.explain: Remain in the car, keep hands on the wheel and follow the officer's instructions.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Proper Action When Stopped by Law Enforcement' (p. 21)

questions.q: Your proof of insurance is in the glove box when an officer asks for it. What should you do?
options: Get out and go to the trunk
Tell the officer where it is and follow their directions before reaching for it
questions.explain: Inform the officer where the items are before retrieving them.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Proper Action When Stopped by Law Enforcement' (p. 21)

questions.q: An unmarked car signals you to pull over and you cannot confirm it is the police. What does the handbook suggest?
options: Drive slowly to a well-lit, populated place or police station, turn on hazard lights, or call 911
Stop immediately in the traffic lane
questions.explain: You may drive carefully to a safe public place or police station, use hazard lights, or call 911.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 4 Traffic Laws, 'Proper Action When Stopped by Law Enforcement' (p. 21)

questions.q: Your vehicle breaks down on a high-capacity road such as an expressway. What is the recommended action?
options: Pull as far right as possible, stay inside with your seat belt on, turn on hazards, and call 911
Get out and walk along the expressway for help
Stop in the lane and raise the hood
Stand behind the vehicle to warn traffic
questions.explain: On high-capacity roads, remain buckled in the vehicle with hazards on and call for help.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Stranded Motorists' Safety Protocols' (p. 90)

questions.q: On the Illinois Tollway, what number can a stranded motorist call besides 911?
questions.explain: Stranded Tollway motorists can call *999 or 911.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Stranded Motorists' Safety Protocols' (p. 90)

questions.q: Your tire blows out at highway speed. What should you do?
options: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and pull off safely without braking suddenly
questions.explain: Ease off the accelerator, keep a firm grip and pull off safely; do not brake suddenly.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Equipment Failure' (p. 88)

questions.q: Your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor. What should you try first?
options: Pump the brake pedal to build pressure
Steer onto the shoulder at full speed
questions.explain: Pump the pedal; if that fails, use the parking brake and shift to a lower gear.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Equipment Failure' (p. 89)

questions.q: Your gas pedal sticks and won't free up with your toe. What should you do?
options: Shift into neutral and brake gently
Turn off the ignition and remove the key
questions.explain: If the pedal stays stuck, shift to neutral and brake gently.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Equipment Failure' (p. 89)

questions.q: You lose power steering control. Why shouldn't you turn off the ignition?
options: The steering may lock or lose power-assist completely
It is illegal to turn off a moving car
questions.explain: Turning off the ignition can lock the steering or remove power assist; ease off the gas and use flashers.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Equipment Failure' (p. 89)

questions.q: Smoke comes from under your hood while driving. What should you do?
options: Pull off the road, turn off the engine, move away from the vehicle and call 911
Keep driving to a service station
Open the hood to fight the fire
questions.explain: Vehicle fires are dangerous; get clear and call 911 rather than fighting it yourself.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 88)

questions.q: A power line falls on your car after a crash, and there is no fire. What should you do?
options: Try to move the wire off the car
Touch the door to test for current
Stay in the vehicle until help arrives
questions.explain: Remain inside unless fire forces you out; then jump clear without touching car and ground at once, and shuffle away 50 feet.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 88)

questions.q: Your car goes into water but does not sink right away. What is the best escape?
options: Wait for the car to fill with water
Call for help and stay seated
questions.explain: Water pressure may keep doors shut; try a window. If sinking, move to the rear air pocket and exit through a rear window.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 88)

questions.q: You approach a crash involving a truck with a hazardous materials placard. What should you do?
options: Stay away and follow emergency responders' directions; report it from a safe place if no responders are there
Get close to read the placard
questions.explain: Avoid the area, follow responders, and seek medical help if you later feel ill.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 9 Roadway Signs, 'Hazardous Materials Signs' (p. 75)

questions.q: How long may a disabled vehicle be left on an interstate or toll highway before police may have it towed?
questions.explain: On interstates, expressways and toll highways, vehicles may be towed after two hours.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 5 Sharing the Road, 'Disabled Vehicles' (p. 45)

questions.q: If your vehicle breaks down on an expressway, what should you never do?
questions.explain: Pull off, raise the hood and turn on flashers; never walk along the expressway.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 11 Safe Driving Tips, 'Special Driving Situations and Hazards' (p. 86)

questions.q: An Illinois car's foot brake must be able to stop it from 20 mph within what distance?
questions.explain: The foot brake must stop a vehicle from 20 mph within 30 feet; the parking brake within 55 feet.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: Your vehicle's taillights must be visible from how far behind?
questions.explain: Two red taillights visible for 500 feet are required.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: Turn signals on a car must be visible from what distance?
questions.explain: Front and rear turn signals must be visible from 300 feet.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: A car's horn must be audible from at least how far away?
questions.explain: Illinois requires a working horn audible from at least 200 feet away.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: Your rear-view mirror must let you see at least how far behind your car?
questions.explain: At least one mirror must show 200 feet to the rear.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: What window tinting is allowed on a front windshield in Illinois?
options: Full tint if you have a medical note for any reason
Only a 6-inch strip along the top
questions.explain: Tinting the front windshield is not allowed except a 6-inch strip along the top.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: A load extends 4 feet or more beyond the rear of your vehicle during the day. What must you display?
options: A red flag at the end of the load
questions.explain: Loads extending 4 feet or more must have a red flag by day and a red light visible 500 feet at night.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Restricted Equipment' (p. 93)

questions.q: May a television or video screen visible from the driver's seat be on while the vehicle is moving?
options: Yes, if the sound is off
questions.explain: Video screens visible to the driver are prohibited while the vehicle is in motion.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Restricted Equipment' (p. 93)

questions.q: The license plate light must make the rear plate readable from how far away?
questions.explain: A white plate light must make the plate readable from 50 feet when headlights are on.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Required Equipment' (p. 92)

questions.q: How many license plates must an Illinois passenger car display?
options: Two, one on the front and one on the rear
None if a temporary permit is in the window
questions.explain: Passenger vehicles, trucks and vans must display front and rear plates.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 13 Owning a Vehicle, 'License Plate Requirements' (p. 96)

questions.q: Which lights visible from the front of a passenger car are prohibited?
questions.explain: Red lights visible from the front are only for police and designated emergency vehicles.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 12 Equipment for Safe Driving, 'Restricted Equipment' (p. 93)

questions.q: When you sell your vehicle in Illinois, what happens to the license plates?
options: They go to the buyer's insurer
The seller removes and keeps them
questions.explain: In Illinois plates stay with the owner, not the vehicle.
questions.ref: Illinois Rules of the Road (2026), Ch. 13 Owning a Vehicle, 'License Plate Requirements' (p. 96)
